summary: Daniel John Gogerly (1792–1862) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He ran the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818–1823), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society in 1838, and served as Secretary, vice-president, and President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1845–1858).

Daniel L. Overmyer (1935–2021) worked in Sinology and religious studies. Educated at Westmar College, Evangelical Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, Joseph Kitagawa, and Philip A. Kuhn, he was a long-time professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2001).

Daniel M. Neuman (born 1944) works in Indology and ethnomusicology. Educated at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago, he held posts at Dartmouth College (1971–1980), University of Washington (1980–1995), and University of California, Los Angeles (~1994–2018).

Daniel M. Stuart works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt, later serving as Assistant Professor at the University of South Carolina and as Gastprofessor at the University of Hamburg.

Daniel M. Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University in 1999, and later held a post at California State University, Chico.
Daniel P. Brown (1948–2022) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Geshe Wangyal. He served as a professor at Harvard Medical School from circa 1980 to 2022.

Daniel R. Tuzzeo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his graduate thesis research at Florida State University under the supervision of Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger (1904–1972) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1922–1925) and later held a post at Princeton University (~1966–1972).

Daniel Sperber (born 1940) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London (~1963–1968), among other institutions, and held posts at Bar-Ilan University from circa 1968 and at the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert P. Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago.

Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of Tasmania, having studied under Parimal G. Patil, Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as an instructor in 2010 alongside a teaching post at Mary Baldwin University.

Daniela Berti specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD in Research Methodology in Ethno-Anthropology from the University of Siena and was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya in 2004.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and was attested as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London in 2020.
Daniele Cuneo is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has held academic posts attested at Sorbonne University in 2018 and as faculty at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.
Danielle Feller specializes in Indology. She completed her PhD in 2001 at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst, and also studied under Ganesh Umakant Thite.

Danielle Jacquart (born 1947) is a scholar in history and archaeology. She studied at the École des chartes (~1967–1971) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1990 to 2016.
Danping Long works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. She is attested in 2026 as a doctoral student at both the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Danuta Stasik (born 1956) is an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1974–1979) and under Maria Krzysztof Byrski (~1979–1989). She has held academic positions at the University of Warsaw, including in 1979 and 1986.

Dasharatha Sharma (1903–1976) was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Delhi. He held posts at the University of Delhi, Hindu College, Jai Narain Vyas University (1966), and directed the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1970–1974).
